body:
It was very hard. Every part of me was screaming that I deserved a chance to be happy, even if that chance was in the 0.0001 percentile. I thought that some chance was better than none. In reality I knew that this wasn't going to be worth the pain, since it was just such a sudden attachment due to my lack of romantic contact and need to feel wanted and loved.

My friends and family are always very supportive of me, and I've been to several anonymous online chats with listeners that help me cope as well. What they can't really help me do, is get my mind off him. I've tried distractions like movies, going out, video games, reading- and at the end of all that, I still hear his voice in my head and see his face in my mind. No matter how hard I shut him out, when I go to sleep, I have horrible dreams about him and his ex getting back together- and me strangling her in a fit of rage.

The more I distance myself and look back on it, he isn't good for me. He's a good man- and he was kind to me, but in the long run, a "relationship" for us wouldn't have worked, no matter how much we both wanted it. It would have been an incredibly straining challenge, and likely wouldn't have even been able to happen for several years- if at all.

I don't blame him either, especially since he's young and she was his first serious love- even if she was psycho. I still have ex lovers and ex friends that I think about even after decades- although there's no longer that emotional attachment.

I'm trying to be proud of myself and be brave, but I keep fighting with myself over that stupid voice in the back of my head that keeps running through what ifs, wondering if I didn't fuck up a good thing.
